newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard proposes new Australian govt code.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard proposes new Australian govt code.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said he wanted to change the government's code of conduct to give ministers a way of holding shares without infringing on the propriety of them being members of the government.

"It is therefore my intention to examine the feasibility of introducing into the arrangements that apply in this country what is categorised in other jurisdictions as the notion of a blind trust," Howard told parliament.
That would allow people with substantial non-real estate assets could put themselves at arms length from the control of those assets.
Government senator Jim Short quit as assistant treasurer on Sunday after his office discovered he had granted a banking license to a subsidiary of a bank in which he held shares.
Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer Brian Gibson resigned on Tuesday, explaining that he had made a decision in June benefitting a company in which he holds shares.
The opposition has criticised two other ministers, Treasurer Peter Costello and, especially, Industry Minister John Moore over having an interest in companies connected with their portfolios.
